items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Freeman opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which many of us are gathered today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishnaabe and Chonnonton peoples. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous people with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Councillor Freeman provided Council with a moment of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

items.title: Items Removed From the Consent Motion
Eby Farm Playground Expansion –
notes: Prepared By: Hala Al Amine and Amy Ross
Hala Al Amine gave a presentation outlining the plans for the expansion of the playground. Amy Ross spoke about the importance of accessible play spaces for all members of the community.

Paula Saunders, Chair, Built Environment Subcommittee, GRAAC spoke about how pleased she was that GRAAC was included in the planning of the new expansion, and the importance of trying to make things accessible for as many people as possible. She then responded to questions of Council. Hala Al Amine also responded to questions of Council.

items.title: 2024 Asset Management Plan
notes: Cassandra Pacey gave a presentation sharing the asset management plan highlights and some of the background of why asset management plans were created, the plan improvements, and the current funding gap. She then responded to questions of Council. Brad Witzel and Ron Ormson also responded to questions of Council.

items.title: 2022 Waterloo Region Community
notes: Ena Ristic introduced Kyra Chisholm, Tova Davidson, and Patrick Gilbride to give their presentation.

Kyra Chisholm, Plan Manager, ClimateActionWR gave a presentation outlining the current progress toward the 50% reduction by 2030 emissions target. She then responded to questions of Council. Tova Davidson, Executive Director, Sustainable WR, Patrick Gilbride, Executive Director, Reep Green Solutions, and Sandy Little also responded to questions of Council.
Alex Latta, Resident of Kitchener spoke about the need for collaboration among local government, organizations in the Region, universities and citizens. He then responded to questions of Council.

Kenneth Epps, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the importance of climate action to the residents of Waterloo, and offered suggestions to Council on how they can better engage with the community. He then responded to questions of Council. Sandy Little and Ena Ristic also responded to questions of Council.
Greg Michalenko, Resident of Waterloo offered some comments surrounding the climate crisis.
Mary Ann Cassidy, Resident of Waterloo spoke about what the City can do to help the residents reduce their greenhouse gas emissions, and promoted a Climate Action Symposium in the fall.

items.title: Indoor Community Space Strategy
notes: Prepared By: Travis McCallum and Beth Rajnovich

Travis McCallum gave a presentation outlining the strategy and the different rounds of engagement used to inform it. He then responded to questions of Council. Beth Rajnovich and Jim Bowman also responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Rental Housing Regulation Review
notes: Prepared By: Grant Curlew, Michelle Lee, and Tanja Curic Grant Curlew gave a presentation outlining the options before Council in the rental licensing review. Michelle Lee continued, speaking about the potential rental eviction regulations. Grant Curlew and Michelle Lee responded to questions of Council.

Theresa Nguyen, Director, Waterloo Undergraduate Student Association spoke in favour of the review. She highlighted the issues faced by those in purpose-built rentals, including the large number of building maintenance requests.

William Pham, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the need to protect student and other vulnerable renters. Nicole Papke responded to question of Council. William Pham also responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Regional All-Council Meeting – June 21, 2024, 2:00 p.m.
notes: Councillor Roe mentioned that World Refugee Day Waterloo Region takes place on Saturday, June 22 at TheMuseum in Kitchener. She highlighted that the second half of that event was a Walk with Refugees from TheMuseum to the Multicultural Centre, where they would be listening to the refugees talking about their experiences.
Councillor Bodaly highlighted that the Friends of Waterloo Park hosted a Summer Start event on Saturday, June 15, with live music and giving away trees.

Councillor Wright noted a couple of Pride related activities that took place in the past week. Spectrum’s Gala was on June 13, 2024 at the Regional Museum, and it was a sold-out event. Cowboys and Angels held a street party on Princess Street to celebrate their 25th anniversary to support Spectrum. She also noted that the Canadian Music Association had their Ontario Music Awards, which celebrated a number of local musicians including Shane Guse, who was awarded Musician of the Year, and Shawn Moore, who was awarded Record Producer of the Year.

Councillor Vasic attended the Grand River Black Music Festival and Conference on June 14-16. She noted that she was excited to see Jully Black perform. She shared that the Conference highlighted and celebrated black music and spoke to some of the challenges that black musicians face. Councilor Vasic also mentioned that the participants got a sneak peek of Hip Hop Hope, a documentary about the local hip hop and DJ scene, which opens tomorrow, June 18.

Mayor McCabe mentioned that June 21 was the National Indigenous Peoples Day, where the history, diversity, and resilience of First Nations, Inuit and Metis people in Canada and in our community are recognized and celebrated.

motions.text: 1. That Council approves CORP2024-018; 2. That Council endorses the 2024 Asset Management Plan; and 3. That Council acknowledges the 2023 average annual infrastructure funding gap of $54.3 million ($37.6 million for tax-funded assets and $16.8 million for enterprise-funded assets); and 4. That Council direct staff to continue advocating for environmental sustainability, climate change and sustainable infrastructure grant funding recognizing that funding support from all levels of government is needed to enable the City to reach its corporate GHG emissions reduction targets of 50% by 2030 (2010 baseline) and net-zero by 2050 while maintaining infrastructure to provide valued services to the City; and 5. That Council directs staff to publish the 2024 Asset Management Plan on the City’s website as required by Ontario Regulation 588/17.
motions.text_html:
1. That Council approves CORP2024-018;

2. That Council endorses the 2024 Asset Management Plan; and

3. That Council acknowledges the 2023 average annual infrastructure funding gap of $54.3 million ($37.6 million for tax-funded assets and $16.8 million for enterprise-funded assets); and

4. That Council direct staff to continue advocating for environmental sustainability, climate change and sustainable infrastructure grant funding recognizing that funding support from all levels of government is needed to enable the City to reach its corporate GHG emissions reduction targets of 50% by 2030 (2010 baseline) and net-zero by 2050 while maintaining infrastructure to provide valued services to the City; and

5. That Council directs staff to publish the 2024 Asset Management Plan on the City’s website as required by Ontario Regulation 588/17.

motions.text: 1. That Council approve report COM2024-025. 2. That Council approve the Indoor Community Space Strategy in principle for inclusion and future development as part of the upcoming Sport, Recreation and Leisure Strategy project. 3. That Council direct staff to adopt the amendments to the Indoor Community Space Strategy: a) Change recommendation 1.3 in Section One: Policy and Organizational Recommendations (Spaces For All) from “Engage with Waterloo’s diverse communities when redesigning or designing a facility” to “Conduct culturally appropriate engagement sessions with diverse communities to identify needs and desired features in existing building retrofits and new builds, and incorporate this input into design standards to inform future projects.” b) Change recommendation 3.5 in Section Three: Building for the Future (Dedicated Arts and Creative Facility) from “Explore opportunities for provision of space for arts and creative industries” to “Prioritize opportunities for provision of space for arts and creative industries.”

motions.text: 1. That Council approve report COM2024-023. 2. That Council direct staff to review the current rental licensing regulations and return to Council with recommendations and, if determined to be appropriate, proposed regulations, in accordance with section 2A of this report. 3. That Council direct staff to complete further research and consultation, including municipal peer review, on a Short-Term Rental (STR) licensing program and return to Council with recommendations and, if determined to be appropriate, proposed regulations, in accordance with section 2B of this report. 4. That Council direct staff to complete further research and consultation, including municipal peer review, on a mid-rise and high-rise safety inspection program and return to Council with proposed regulations, if determined to be appropriate, in accordance with section 2C of this report. 5. That Council direct staff to consider the feasibility and merits of allocating a portion of the Affordable Housing Reserve to support existing tenant support programs (Item #3 in section 2D of this report) and to return to Council with recommended next steps. 6. That Council direct staff to explore the relative costs and benefits of funding an eviction regulation program versus funding a longer-term City’s Multi-Unit Residential Acquisition (MURA) program (Item #4 in section 2D of this report); and return to Council with additional information and recommend next steps.
motions.text_html:
1. That Council approve report COM2024-023.

2. That Council direct staff to review the current rental licensing regulations and return to Council with recommendations and, if determined to be appropriate, proposed regulations, in accordance with section 2A of this report.

3. That Council direct staff to complete further research and consultation, including municipal peer review, on a Short-Term Rental (STR) licensing program and return to Council with recommendations and, if determined to be appropriate, proposed regulations, in accordance with section 2B of this report.

4. That Council direct staff to complete further research and consultation, including municipal peer review, on a mid-rise and high-rise safety inspection program and return to Council with proposed regulations, if determined to be appropriate, in accordance with section 2C of this report.

5. That Council direct staff to consider the feasibility and merits of allocating a portion of the Affordable Housing Reserve to support existing tenant support programs (Item #3 in section 2D of this report) and to return to Council with recommended next steps.

6. That Council direct staff to explore the relative costs and benefits of funding an eviction regulation program versus funding a longer-term City’s Multi-Unit Residential Acquisition (MURA) program (Item #4 in section 2D of this report); and return to Council with additional information and recommend next steps.
